**Page:** Hurricane Ian (2022) Tropical Cyclone Report – https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/AL092022_Ian.pdf  

**Evidence**  
- **Event:** Hurricane Ian (2022)  
  - “Hurricane IAN (AL092022) 23‑30 September 2022”  
- **Location/Impact region:**  
  - “Ian made landfall in southwestern Florida at category 4 intensity … Ian was responsible for over 150 direct and indirect deaths … Ian also made landfall as a category 3 hurricane in western Cuba … Ian made its final landfall near Georgetown, South Carolina.”  
- **Direct fatalities in the United States:**  
  - “In the United States, Ian was responsible for at least 156 fatalities, 66 of which were considered deaths directly caused by the storm.” (p. 12)  
  - “All direct deaths in the United States occurred in Florida (Fig. 16).” (p. 12)  
  - “Storm surge was the deadliest hazard, claiming 41 lives, with 36 of the 41 surge fatalities occurring in Lee County, Florida.” (p. 12)  
  - “There were 12 direct fatalities attributed to freshwater flooding in central and eastern Florida, 8 were categorized as marine fatalities, 4 were related to wind, and 1 was due to rough surf.” (p. 12)  
  - “A boat carrying a reported 27 migrants … capsized … only 7 bodies were recovered (accounting for 7 of the 8 marine deaths).” (p. 12)  
- **Indirect (non‑direct) fatalities in the United States:**  
  - “Ian was also indirectly responsible for 90 casualties in the United States.” (p. 13)  
  - “Most of the victims (84 in total) were located in Florida, with 5 in North Carolina, and 1 in Virginia.” (p. 13)  
  - Causes of indirect deaths: 18 lack of access to timely medical care; 16 accidents (trip‑and‑fall during power outages); 16 cardiac events; other causes include vehicular accidents, accidents related to storm preparations or clean up, carbon monoxide poisoning, suicide, and homicide. (p. 13)

- Total fatalities (direct and indirect);  
- Breakdown by direct vs. indirect;  
- Geographic distribution of direct deaths (all Florida);  
- Geographic distribution of indirect deaths (Florida 84, North Carolina 5, Virginia 1);  
- Detailed causes of direct deaths;  
- Storm surge fatalities.  

The list is **complete for the 2022 Hurricane Ian casualty data**. No other years or storms are covered.

- Identification of states impacted by 2023 storm(s) that sustained casualties.
